rationale: Inbox intake of the founder's second essay, 'Knots of Existence Hypotheses' (Eugene Jhong, Substack, 2026-09-08, text generated wholly by Fable 5.1). The item is marked NEW TO THE LEDGER AND SUPPLIED BY ITS AUTHOR, so it enters as a provisional Source record labelled for what it is — a self-published, AI-generated hypothesis essay by the case's proponent — and its distinct testable propositions are catalogued as unfeatured, ungraded claims anchored to it by page, for the editions to weigh. The essay's central move is a competing account of the anchor phenomenon: knots as cutaneous perforators (artery–nerve–lymphatic bundles through fascial rings) held in a stuck state, breath-gated by the inspiratory vasoconstrictor reflex, collared by gelled hyaluronan, tethering a continuous superficial-fascial sheet — an alternative to the ledger's intramuscular latched-arteriole attribution (VASO-C020), linked with alternativeToRefs rather than merged. A second family of reports (sheet separation, folds, hollows, air) is catalogued as mechanism claims with the essay's own physician's-road alternative (hyperventilation paresthesia) entered as a competing claim. Where the essay restates published findings (Heine, Dorsher, Langevin, Segal & Duling, Hong & Simons, Taylor & Palmer, Lindahl, Sikdar, Moraska, Cagnie, Fede), the propositions enter as claims anchored to the essay and as weak/context evidence toward existing claims, with limitations stating that no primary was retrieved. Every one of the 39 works the report lists as 'no OpenAlex result' is dispositioned: four are ledger duplicates, most are blocked with a retrieval route, two are irrelevant. Where a proposition already exists in the index (fascial densification reversibility, VASO-C077; cascade, VASO-C065; blood-first, VASO-C073), the essay's passage enters as evidence or as a refining child claim rather than a new duplicate. No corrections: no source text was reached at a URL. Edition unchanged: the pass adds hypothesis material and secondary restatements, not a load-bearing finding; the current telling remains correct, and the perforator alternative should be weighed at the next assessment once its primaries are retrieved. Nothing is graded here.

sources.identifier: Substack essay dated 2026-09-08 (author byline 'EUGENE'; © 2026 Eugene Jhong); text states 'Text generated wholly by Fable 5.1'; supplied by the author as PDF, 41 pages, research/vasocomputation/knots-of-existence-hypotheses.pdf; no URL shown to this pass
reliabilityNotes: Self-published essay by the case founder and hypothesis proponent; not peer-reviewed.
Text generated wholly by an AI model (Fable 5.1) at the author's direction, per p. 1.
Hypothesis material: takes practitioner reports 'as true' by stated rule (p. 3); its statements about published studies are secondary restatements whose primaries were not retrieved this pass.
Pipeline text extraction truncates the right margin of many lines; quotations were taken from intact words only.

evidence.title: Second essay relocates the vascular element from intramuscular arterioles to cutaneous perforators
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that the perforator model moves the vascular hypothesis to the arterioles of the skin and superficial fascia and 'relocates the vascular hypothesis rather than rescuing it'.
evidence.editorInference: A proponent's own statement of a competing account; it carries no diagnostic weight on VASO-C020 but records that the hypothesis's author no longer treats the intramuscular arteriole as the primary site.
limitations: AI-generated self-published essay by the proponent; no measurement reported.

evidence.title: Second essay accepts the arteriole audit: sustained activation, not economical latch
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that published measurements in pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles 'show sustained activation rather than an economical latch', calling this a mismatch rather than a refutation.
evidence.editorInference: This restates the ledger's own study (VASO-E020) back to it; it adds no independent observation.

evidence.title: Proponent's essay drops the latch as a load-bearing part
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that under the perforator model the thesis 'loses the latch as a load-bearing part' and with it the metabolic-cold-spot prediction as a necessary signature.
evidence.editorInference: The author of the hypothesis narrows what VASO-C020 must claim; a qualifier on the claim's scope from its own side, not evidence about tissue.

evidence.title: Essay restates Hong & Simons 1993: inactivating a key trigger point inactivated its satellites
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay reports that Hong and Simons found that 'inactivating a key trigger point inactivated its satellites without treating them' (1993), offered as a clinical demonstration of upstream dependence among knots.
evidence.editorInference: Second-hand; the primary was not retrieved. If accurate it is the closest published analogue to the cascade claim, but it concerns needling, not breath-assisted release.
limitations: Secondary restatement in an AI-generated essay; primary not retrieved.

evidence.title: Essay restates Lindahl 2017: most common somatic report was tension building then releasing, with positive affect
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay reports that the largest study of meditation-related experiences found the most common somatic report was 'pressure or tension that built and then released', with release associated with positive affect, surges of energy and involuntary movements (Lindahl et al. 2017).
evidence.editorInference: Second-hand; the primary was not retrieved. It concerns meditators' reports, not knot release under pressure, so it bears on VASO-C091 only by analogy.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primary not retrieved; different population and practice.

evidence.title: Essay restates Moraska 2013 and Cagnie 2012: local blood-flow rises after compression or needling
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states 'Release brings blood: with microdialysis catheter inside an active trigger point' ischemic compression produced a transient rise in local blood flow (Moraska et al. 2013), and that a dry-needling stimulus raised blood flow and oxygen saturation at the needled site for fifteen minutes (Cagnie et al. 2012), the latter in healthy volunteers.
evidence.editorInference: Neither study times perfusion against stiffness, so neither bears on the ordering VASO-C073 asserts; background only. Primaries not retrieved.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primaries not retrieved; no stiffness measurement in either study as described.

evidence.title: Essay restates Sikdar 2009: hypoechoic, stiffer nodules with abnormal flow at trapezius trigger points
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay reports that Sikdar and colleagues, using gray-scale ultrasound, vibration sonoelastography and Doppler on upper-trapezius trigger points, 'found discrete hypoechoic nodules, stiffer than the surrounding' tissue with abnormal flow around them.
evidence.editorInference: Same NIH lineage as SRC-BALLYNS-2011 (VASO-E022–E023); not independent of it. Primary not retrieved.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primary not retrieved; not independent of the Ballyns 2011 records.

evidence.title: Essay restates an attenuated skin blood-flow response over latent trigger points
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that Arendt-Nielsen's group reported 'an attenuated skin blood-flow response over latent trigger points', which it calls the first hint of a cutaneous vasomotor abnormality at a knot.
evidence.editorInference: This is the Zhang 2009 finding already dispositioned as blocked; the essay's restatement adds no text from the primary.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primary (Zhang et al. 2009) not retrieved.

evidence.title: Essay restates equine needle-EMG: same spontaneous activity as human trigger points
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that needle electromyography of trigger points in the equine cleidobrachialis 'found the same spontaneous activity the human studies report'.
evidence.editorInference: Cross-species background; it says nothing about the endplate-zone prevalence gradient VASO-C002 asserts. Primary not retrieved.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primary (Macgregor & von Schweinitz 2006) not retrieved.

evidence.title: Essay: both roads agree the tender points change within a session — state, not scar
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that its perforator model and the physician's conventional account both say the tender points are real 'and change within a session — state, not scar'.
evidence.editorInference: A proponent asserting common ground; the premise (objective within-session change) is precisely what the ledger has not measured, so this is weightless on VASO-C011.

evidence.title: Essay restates Heine 1988: most classical acupoints sit where a neurovascular bundle perforates the superficial fascia
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay reports that Heine (1988) dissected and found about eighty percent of the classical 'points coincide with sites where a neurovascular bundle perforates the superficial' fascia, and that Dorsher put trigger-point/acupoint anatomical correspondence above ninety percent.
evidence.editorInference: Second-hand; primaries not retrieved. Even if accurate these are post-hoc anatomical correspondences without a chance baseline, and they concern acupoints, not the rtsa mdud or granthi maps VASO-C022 names.
limitations: Secondary restatement; primaries not retrieved; no blinded coding or chance baseline described; the essay itself notes a contrary dissection (Maurer et al. 2019).

evidence.title: Essay restates the densification model: hyaluronan gel reversed by warmth, acid washout and shear
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that the loose tissue around a perforator is rich in hyaluronan, which gels when the tissue turns acidic and cool, and that 'it is reversed by warmth, by washout of acid, and by shear'.
evidence.editorInference: Restatement of the Stecco-group concept with no timescale given; the seconds-scale question VASO-R008 asks remains open.
limitations: Secondary, uncited at that passage; no reversal timescale stated.

research.title: Map the staples: blinded coincidence of palpated tender points with pencil-Doppler perforators against chance
research.summary: One blinded examiner marks tender points on a region of scalp, neck, back or hip; a second blinded operator maps cutaneous perforators on the same region by continuous-wave pencil Doppler at fixed light pressure; a third computes spatial coincidence against a chance baseline from randomized point sets. Settles whether ordinary knots sit on perforators (VASO-C101) and whether the most tender sit on the largest trunks; a null returns the vascular hypothesis to the intramuscular compartment or dissolves it.
research.informationGain: A cheap, afternoon-scale test that either licenses or kills the perforator alternative before any imaging is bought; a positive coincidence above chance would be the first objective anatomical identity for a palpated knot.

research.title: Film a star: laser speckle over a superficial knot with exhale, inhale-hold, sham-site and CO2 controls
research.summary: Laser speckle contrast imaging over the occiput or upper trapezius during breath-assisted release; mark a knot and a sham site, record respiration, end-tidal CO2, surface EMG and a button press at each felt release; apply calibrated pressure on exhale and, in matched trials, during an inhale-and-hold. Preregistered predictions: local perfusion flash time-locked to exhale and button, absent at sham and under inhale-hold (perforator account); versus global changes tracking CO2 (hyperventilation account).
research.informationGain: Directly discriminates the perforator, hyperventilation and no-local-event accounts of the felt release at the surface, where no depth problem exists, and tests the blood-first ordering with a non-contact method.

research.title: Free a collar without breath: ultrasound-guided saline hydrodissection at a mapped perforator under a tender point
research.summary: In a clinic already performing nerve hydrodissection, place a few milliliters of saline around a Doppler-mapped perforator at its fascial ring beneath a blinded-examiner tender point, with no breath instruction and no manual pressure; record tenderness (algometry), the felt star, and elastography before and after; sham injection adjacent to the bundle as control.
research.informationGain: The cleanest single test of the collared-perforator identification: release without breath refutes the two-key necessity (VASO-C039) and supports VASO-C101; no effect leaves the knot with motor guarding or another account.

research.title: The knot-free endpoint as a natural experiment, with a sensory exam to exclude a damaged finder
research.summary: Recruit practitioners who report having completed the release process; blinded examiner, standardized sites, pressure algometry, light-touch and pinprick sensory exam, Doppler perforator map, elastography, against age-matched controls. A blinded finding of no tender points in a middle-aged adult with normal sensation and normally perfused perforators supports VASO-C124; reduced sensation with constricted perforators supports the hypoesthesia confound VASO-C125.
research.informationGain: Cheap and decisive for the endpoint prediction, and it cannot be gamed by expectation because the sensory exam separates 'no knots' from 'no finder'.

research.title: Open the primaries behind the second essay's audit (Heine 1988; Langevin & Yandow 2002; Dorsher 2009; Segal & Duling 1986; Hong & Simons 1993; Taylor & Palmer 1987; Lindahl 2017; Sikdar 2009; Moraska 2013; Cagnie 2012; Fede 2022)
